subject: Capacity sprint timeline & ops binder for DEAL-4382
messages:
From: Sapphire OEM <procurement@sapphire-oem.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>; Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionsys.com>
Cc: AtlasCloud Solutions <cloud-ops@atlascloud.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HW availability window for Orion Systems / preliminary ETA

Hi Nikhil / Tim,

Thanks for the heads-up — attached is our initial quote and a conservative shipping cadence for the GPUs you asked about. Short summary: current allocation shows a Q1 2027 staging window for a tranche of 240 cards and a follow-up Q2 2027 tranche of 360 cards. Leadtimes are driven by wafer backlog + assembly capacity; we can priority-queue a tranche if Orion confirms a minimum commit and a partial prepayment.

Key constraints you should know:
- Allocation is split across two fabs (APAC/EMEA); cross-dock will add ~7–14 days.
- BOM revision requested by OEM customers in September pushed some shipments out by 3–4 weeks.
- We can attribute a reserved lane if redlines on the PO are accepted within 10 business days.

Attachments: Sapphire-quote-v1.pdf (PDF), leadtime-table.csv (CSV)

If helpful I can run a fast-track availability check but I need an estimated monthly consumption number from you for Q1.

Regards,
Lena Morales
Head of Strategic Accounts, Sapphire OEM
[attachment: Sapphire-quote-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Lena Morales <procurement@sapphire-oem.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionsys.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HW availability window for Orion Systems / preliminary ETA

Lena — thanks for the quick turnaround and the quote. Attaching a compact matrix (Capacity-sprint-matrix.xlsx) that maps Orion's committed ramp by month to required card counts; that should give you the monthly consumption signal you asked for.

Top asks from our side so we can finalize an execution path:
1) Can you provide a stamped allocation promise (email OK) for the Q1 tranche contingent on a 30% deposit and PO within 7 business days? We need to show Orion the reservation to close the deal.
2) If you can priority-queue, what is the firm earliest ship week and the margin of error (± weeks)?
3) Are there alternate SKUs you can ship now (slightly lower perf quantization-friendly) that would work as a temporary backstop while the main SKU ships?

Operational notes: AtlasCloud has agreed to be our cloud backstop for the first 8 weeks post-ship if there are customs or port delays; cc'd Andrew's team on the specifics. Ben — please flag any procurement constraints on prepayment/escrow. Karthik — want you to review the matrix and propose a staging + burn rate plan that keeps latency SLAs within target while we stagger ingestion.

Thanks — Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Dedicated Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Capacity-sprint-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>; Lena Morales <procurement@sapphire-oem.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionsys.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HW availability window for Orion Systems / preliminary ETA

Nikhil / Lena — I reviewed the matrix and sketched an ops-runbook. High level:

- Staging plan: Receive Q1 tranche at our Oregon staging site; run fast burn-in + image push within 5 business days. That yields a live capacity window of ~10 business days post-ship if customs are smooth.
- Hybrid fallback: Deploy a mixed-pool config where 30% of workload is routed to AtlasCloud class-B instances (lower cost/longer tails) while we finish onboarding remaining cards.
- SKU fallback: If Sapphire can supply the quant-friendly SKU (Sapphire-QF-8) in November in smaller volume, we can provision an interim channel for L1 customers; performance delta is acceptable for 75% of targeted workloads.

Operational asks for acceptance:
A) A written allocation confirmation for Q1 tranche with expected ship-week and list of shipped SKUs (including serial ranges).
B) A commitment from AtlasCloud on the burst capacity API and egress pricing (cc'd).
C) Procurement: clarify payment milestone structure (30% deposit, 50% on ship, 20% on acceptance).

I'll put the runbook into Confluence after Lena confirms the dates so we can coordinate on port/clearance hold times.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Hardware Orchestration, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Morales <procurement@sapphire-oem.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tim Chen <tim.chen@orionsys.com>, AtlasCloud Solutions <cloud-ops@atlascloud.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 00:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HW availability window for Orion Systems / preliminary ETA

Nikhil / team — quick update after internal sync: we can firm the Q1 tranche to a ship-week of 2027-01-18 (estimated) if we receive a PO and the 30% deposit by 2026-11-16. Margin of error is ±2 weeks given current fab schedules.

Alternate path: we can stage an interim shipment of up to 80 cards (Sapphire-QF-8) out of our APAC line with ETA late-November; leadtime for that SKU is shorter because it uses available inventory. Pricing is slightly higher (see quote line 3).

We will prepare an allocation confirmation email once you confirm the payment milestones. For customs and cross-dock, AtlasCloud's approach to egress looks fine; we'll list the cross-dock buffer in the allocation email.

Next steps (action items):
- Orion (Tim) to confirm the deal PO approval and bank details for the deposit by 2026-11-12.
- Nikhil to confirm which tranche we prioritize (Q1 full vs Q1 + interim 80-card shipment).
- Karthik to publish the staging runbook after we receive allocation confirmation.

I'll send the stamped allocation email once the PO condition is satisfied.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Morales
Head of Strategic Accounts, Sapphire OEM
